propositions: The inbound-probe dispatch chain has no live producer because differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes iterates local_state with jira_key fields, but run_differs passes prev_snapshot (a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries carry no jira_key), making the loop never emit and everything downstream dead.

Deletion discrimination is already implemented twice in production and verified live on DC: outbound_differ._safe_get_issue and binding_walk.py:187-196 both perform bounded direct GET→404 confirmation; the dead inbound-probe arm is a vestige of an earlier design.

A retired binding (confirmed 404 after grace) causes the local ticket to become unbound, after which outbound_differ emits CREATE for it, resurrecting the deliberately-deleted Jira issue on a 3-pass delay; prior art (Unito, Kubernetes) rejects such resurrection by design.

The tombstone guard prevents unbound-local CREATE when a retired binding exists for that local ticket, blocking resurrection of confirmed-deleted pairings while permitting creation of never-bound local tickets.

The resurrection implementation (create_after_hard_delete, _apply_inbound_delete, route_inbound_probe, _build_hard_delete_recreate) is removed rather than orphaned, and the dead producer chain is deleted along with its fixture-only test.
